content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends; true prices often dip below forecast before rebounding.
- Forecasting horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is positive, especially in early days of the forecast window.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds high forecasts too long after sharp spikes, ignoring recent price pullback signals.
- When sentiment turns negative, model delays correction and overestimates downside risk, leading to overcorrection later.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in the first 10 days of the 30d window — model reacts too slowly to sentiment shifts.
